chapter: Kansas City rooms and Piney Brown
title: How Piney treated musicians and how he died
summary: He paid the same scale but stuffed money into musicians' clothes; he fell ill and died on the West Coast.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: He took good care of his musicians.
Paid probably more than other owners in town?
Except he laid it off on tips?

-- except he would give you money. He'd come in a joint where you were playing when he knew you and he would stuff money in your clothes or anything, you know. "Come on and have a drink", and he was -- as I say, he was about the biggest spender in this man's town, Kansas City, Missouri.
And you liked him, not only for the money but I mean --
Everybody. You had to like him.
You trusted him and you liked him?
Right, right. He never would do anything, you know, where it would hurt you. I just -- with some of the others, he was a man that loved life and lived life.
How did he die? Did he die a natural death?
No. He went to open up a big policy thing on the West Coast but this venture never did happen because soon he fell ill and he died out on the West Coast.
